+def merge(ids, pair, idx):
+    """
+    In the list of integers (ids), replace all consecutive occurrences
+    of pair with the new integer token idx
+    Example: ids=[1, 2, 3, 1, 2], pair=(1, 2), idx=4 -> [4, 3, 4]
+    """
+    newids = []
+    append = newids.append
+    i = 0
+    n = len(ids)
+    last = n - 1
+    p0, p1 = pair
+    while i < last:
+        # if the pair matches, replace it
+        if ids[i] == p0 and ids[i+1] == p1:
+            append(idx)
+            i += 2
+        else:
+            append(ids[i])
+            i += 1
+    if i == last:
+        append(ids[i])
+    return newids
+

actions.reason: Move the merge helpers' last-element handling out of the main scan loop. The loop now only scans positions that can start a pair, avoiding the per-iteration end-of-list check while preserving the same output for unmatched trailing tokens.
